title: Add a blocking CI check that rejects Dockerfile FROM lines without an @sha256 digest
description: Add a job to applications/mcp-gateway/repos/mongodb-mcp-server/.github/workflows/check.yml that runs on pull_request and push to main. It finds every Dockerfile in the repo and fails when a `FROM` line references an image without `@sha256:` (allow `FROM scratch` and references to earlier build stages). Pin any third-party action it uses to a full commit SHA, as docker-publish.yml already does. Make the check required for main in branch protection so a later edit cannot reintroduce a floating base image. Merge through the normal PR process with 1 approval. This change does not touch runtime images.
acceptanceCriteria: A PR on main that changes either Dockerfile back to `FROM node:24-alpine` fails the new check, with a message that names the file and line
The same check passes on main after tasks 1 and 2 are merged, and branch protection for main lists it as a required status check

verificationMethod.description: Open a throwaway draft PR that removes the @sha256 digest from deploy/aws/Dockerfile. Expected: the new check.yml job fails and names deploy/aws/Dockerfile. Close the PR unmerged, then confirm the job is green on main and listed under required status checks in the main branch protection settings.

rootCause.description: The CI gates in sdlc/policy.json (sast, secrets, unit-tests) and the repo's check.yml include no base-image pinning check. That is why the floating FROM tags merged unnoticed, and nothing stops them from coming back.
